text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The government is determined to prove that Lithuania is as ready for EU entry as Estonia.
- Doctors had to amputate the arm of a woman after she was attacked by a Rottweiler dog.
- Experts said that the decision of the European Commission to exclude Lithuania from the first wave of eastward expansion was due to duties on EU goods.
- Dealers forecast that the trade in Vilniaus and Hermis bank shares would dominate trade on the bourse.

- Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will attend a conference on good neighbourly relations in Vilnius on Setember 5-6. The conference is expected to be attended by the presidents of Estonia, Latvia, Finland, Poland, Ukraine and Lithuania.
- Russian Orthodox Church Patriarch Aleksey II will start a three-day official visit to Lithuania on Friday.

- Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said in an interview that EU PHARE experts are to decide who will advise on the privatisation of state-run Agricultural Bank. The start of the privatisation of the bank is expected at the beginning of 1998.
- Omnitel and Bite GSM mobile phone operators expect to have over 100,000 clients by the end of the year. The two now have 67,500 clients, 40,000 of them in Omnitel.
- The state energy pricing commission decided to increase electricity prices by 10 percent to 0.22 litas from 0.20 litas.
- Experts said that the sucessfull distribution of a $200 million eurobond will cut the costs of domestic borrowing.
